title: A choice's note argues for it
statement: A note shown beside a choice before the learner picks must give the reason someone might believe that choice, never argue against it, or it gives the answer away.
example: In all four lessons of one live walk, the wrong card's note argued against itself in print before the child tapped.
detail: A live walk of four grade-3 reading lessons played every visible page as one child in one session. Where the three earlier lessons' wrong-card notes argued for the wrong card, all four of these printed a note that argued against it before the child tapped. The walk's fix gives each wrong note the reason a child might believe it, and it records that no check compared a wrong choice's note with its tone.
